metadata.description: CNQ Spark on Ubuntu 22.04 in your subscription, with no public IP. On first boot the VM downloads the Spark bundle, then asks Qumulo for a Core download link that lasts 15 minutes. To get it, the VM sends the email entered here and Microsoft's signed identity document for this VM, which names its VM ID and subscription ID. Qumulo keeps the email, the VM ID, a hash of the subscription ID, the region and the Core version, to count installs.
Linux name. Becomes the Spark cluster name.
Resource id of an existing subnet.
https URL of the Spark bundle. A release pins it.
SHA-256 of the bundle: 64 lowercase hex digits.
Email. Required: Spark sends it to Qumulo with the VM's Azure identity to get Core.
Spark admin password. Delivered by a managed Run Command's protected parameter, never in customData.
Tags by resource type, from the portal form's Tags step. The VM and its network interface take their own; the disks made with the VM take none.

variables.$fxv#0:
#!/bin/bash
# The deploy form's admin password, from the Run Command's protected parameter (never customData).
# Never replaces an existing file, so a re-run can't undo a password changed since.
set -euo pipefail
root=${SPARK_PREFIX:-}
exec python3 - "$root" <<'PY'
import os, re, sys, tempfile
root = sys.argv[1]
pw = os.environ.pop("SPARK_FORM_PASSWORD", "")
ok = 12 <= len(pw) <= 64 and re.fullmatch(r'[!#-\[\]-~]+', pw) and sum(bool(re.search(p, pw)) for p in (r'[a-z]', r'[A-Z]', r'[0-9]', r'[^A-Za-z0-9]')) >= 3
if not ok:
    sys.stderr.write("the admin password breaks Spark's rules\n")
    sys.exit(1)
d = root + "/etc/spark"
path = d + "/admin-password"
prefix = ".admin-password.form-"
try:
    os.makedirs(d, mode=0o755, exist_ok=True)
    for stale in os.listdir(d):  # left by a run killed between mkstemp and unlink
        if stale.startswith(prefix):
            try:
                os.unlink(d + "/" + stale)
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass
    if os.path.exists(path):
        sys.exit(0)
    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=d, prefix=prefix)
    try:
        os.write(fd, pw.encode()); os.fsync(fd); os.close(fd)
        os.chmod(tmp, 0o600)
        os.link(tmp, path)  # fails if a file appeared meanwhile; never replaces
    except FileExistsError:
        pass
    finally:
        os.unlink(tmp)
    dfd = os.open(d, os.O_RDONLY); os.fsync(dfd); os.close(dfd)
except OSError:
    sys.stderr.write("spark: could not write /etc/spark/admin-password\n")
    sys.exit(1)
PY
variables.bootstrap:
#!/bin/bash
# The Spark deploy template's first-boot script. cloud-init runs it once, as
# root, on the VM's first boot. It keeps a root-only copy as
# /usr/local/sbin/spark-bootstrap and, before any network step, a MOTD naming
# the log and that retry command. The template puts the bundle's URL and
# SHA-256, the email, the hostname and the cloud below base64-encoded, so they
# are decoded as data and never read as shell.
set -euo pipefail
url=$(printf '%s' '__BUNDLE_URL_B64__' | base64 -d)
sum=$(printf '%s' '__BUNDLE_SHA256_B64__' | base64 -d)
email=$(printf '%s' '__WORK_EMAIL_B64__' | base64 -d)
# Base64 has no underscore, so a marker still in place is a template older
# than these two (v0.10.1): it gives no hostname and no cloud, and neither
# /etc/spark/hostname nor /etc/spark/cloud is written.
hostname_b64='__HOSTNAME_B64__'
cloud_b64='__CLOUD_B64__'
hostname=$([[ $hostname_b64 == *_* ]] || printf '%s' "$hostname_b64" | base64 -d)
cloud=$([[ $cloud_b64 == *_* ]] || printf '%s' "$cloud_b64" | base64 -d)
# Tests only: a scratch root. Unset on a VM.
root=${SPARK_PREFIX:-}
dir=$root/opt/spark-install
self=$root/usr/local/sbin/spark-bootstrap
tmp=""
unpack=""
# One install at a time: a retry while another runs would delete its unpack
# directory. install.sh inherits the lock through exec and holds it to the end.
install -d -m 0755 "$root/run"
exec 9>"$root/run/spark-bootstrap.lock"
if ! flock -n 9; then
  echo "spark-bootstrap: an install is already running; sudo spark shows its progress" >&2
  exit 1
fi
# A failed download or unpack leaves nothing behind. exec skips this trap, and
# after the rename there is no unpack directory left to remove.
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"; if [[ -n $unpack ]]; then rm -rf "$unpack"; fi' EXIT

install -d -m 0755 "$root/var/log"
exec >>"$root/var/log/spark-install.log" 2>&1
echo "spark-bootstrap: $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
if [[ $(readlink -f "$0") != "$self" ]]; then
  # Root-only: the copy holds the email and the bundle URL.
  install -D -m 0700 "$0" "$self"
fi
# install.sh replaces this with the bundle's 99-spark.
install -d -m 0755 "$root/etc/update-motd.d"
cat > "$root/etc/update-motd.d/99-spark" <<EOF
#!/bin/sh
echo "Spark is still setting up, or setup stopped."
echo "Logs: /var/log/spark-install.log"
echo "Retry: sudo $self"
EOF
chmod 0755 "$root/etc/update-motd.d/99-spark"

# A saved address wins over the template's: editing this file is how a retry
# corrects a refused or malformed email.
install -d -m 0755 "$root/etc/spark"
# A template deploy. On Azure, first-boot.sh waits for the deploy's secret
# instead of generating its own; other clouds ignore the marker. Written
# before the download so it always exists before first-boot.sh runs.
: > "$root/etc/spark/admin-password.from-deploy"
chmod 0644 "$root/etc/spark/admin-password.from-deploy"
if [[ -s $root/etc/spark/install-email ]]; then
  email=$(cat "$root/etc/spark/install-email")
fi
if [[ ! $url =~ ^https://[^[:space:]]+$ || ! $sum =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ || ! $email =~ ^[^[:space:]@]+@[^[:space:]@]+$ ]]; then
  echo "spark-bootstrap: the template needs an https bundle URL, its SHA-256 and an email"
  exit 1
fi
# The hostname is empty or follows the form's VM name rule; a given cloud is
# one short lowercase word (install.sh checks that Spark knows it).
if [[ -n $hostname && ! $hostname =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,13}[a-z0-9]$ ]] ||
  [[ $cloud_b64 != *_* && ! $cloud =~ ^[a-z]{1,16}$ ]]; then
  echo "spark-bootstrap: the template's hostname (2 to 15 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens) or cloud is not valid"
  exit 1
fi
if [[ ! -s $root/etc/spark/install-email ]]; then
  (umask 077 && printf '%s\n' "$email" > "$root/etc/spark/install-email")
fi
# For install.sh, which sets the hostname and picks the cloud's login user;
# without /etc/spark/cloud a VM is on Azure.
if [[ $cloud_b64 != *_* ]]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$cloud" > "$root/etc/spark/cloud"
  chmod 0644 "$root/etc/spark/cloud"
fi
if [[ -n $hostname ]]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$hostname" > "$root/etc/spark/hostname"
  chmod 0644 "$root/etc/spark/hostname"
fi
# The bundle is unpacked beside $dir and renamed into place, so $dir exists
# only when complete. An interrupted run leaves a temp directory; it goes here.
if [[ ! -d $dir ]]; then
  install -d -m 0755 "$(dirname "$dir")"
  rm -rf "$dir".tmp.*
  tmp=$(mktemp)
  unpack=$(mktemp -d "$dir.tmp.XXXXXX")
  # A new subnet may have no outbound access unless it is given a NAT gateway
  # or a firewall route, and this is the first fetch.
  # Only the host is logged: the URL may carry a SAS token or credentials.
  if ! curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' --retry 5 --retry-delay 10 --retry-all-errors \
    --max-time 900 -o "$tmp" "$url"; then
    host=${url#https://}
    host=${host%%[/?#]*}
    host=${host##*@}
    echo "spark-bootstrap: could not download the Spark bundle from $host; check that the subnet has outbound internet access (a NAT gateway or firewall)"
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "$sum  $tmp" | sha256sum -c --quiet -
  tar -xzf "$tmp" -C "$unpack" --no-same-owner
  rm -f "$tmp"
  [[ -x $unpack/install.sh && -x $unpack/spark ]]
  chmod 0755 "$unpack"
  mv "$unpack" "$dir"
  unpack=""
fi
exec "$dir/install.sh"
